newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine strike support lukewarm in capital.
newsitem.headline: Argentine strike support lukewarm in capital.

text.p: Unions manned roadblocks throughout Argentina and closed many provincial firms on Thursday, but support was lukewarm in Buenos Aires for a general strike boycotted by workers loyal to the government.
Union leaders said they had paralyzed the nation and warned the governing Peronists the strike was a foretaste of the anger they would face in October's congressional elections.

"This protest was a rehearsal for the slap in the face to the government that believed in its conceit is going to win in the next elections," Victor De Gennaro, leader of the CTA public sector union, told Reuters.
He said well over half the nation's workers took part in the strike, closing down transportation, schools and the court system as well as sapping industry.

But Labor Minister Armando Caro Figueroa called the strike the least effective of the many President Carlos Menem has faced. He told reporters only 16 percent to 19 percent of workers joined the protest, and he apologized to citizens "whose rights were infringed on" by strike action.
The MTA and CTA opposition unions called the 24-hour strike to protest against Argentina's 16.1 percent unemployment rate and proposed labor market reforms.
But the main union federation, the CGT, has made a deal on labor reforms with the government and opposed the strike.
The grain port of Necochea was closed, and roadblocks cut access to the cities of Rosario and Cordoba, where many businesses closed and public transportation was off the streets.
In Buenos Aires, state schools took a holiday and buses operated at a fifth of the normal level, officials said.

Other transportation, including flights from Ezeiza international airport, was almost normal. With bus services at a trickle, cars clogged roads into the city, and once people arrived, they went to work -- or cafes -- as usual.

A few dozen people at a roadblock lit puddles of gasoline and stoned police in the Isidro Casanova neighborhood on the outskirts of Buenos Aires. Police charged and fired rubber bullets. Six people were injured and two arrested.
